Caveats: secondary tags like X_MIMP/X_ProtMapper credited to X (indirect attribution); PhosphoSitePlus direct download failed (0 entries, likely login-gated), so peptides only for SIGNOR-covered sites; 1,512 SIGNOR rows lacking a residue were excluded.
final_answer:
Atlas accepted: 40,156 human kinase|substrate|site entries. 3 of the 40,159 I built were dropped by the harness as invalid; I did not identify which ones.

Sources:
1. OmniPath enzyme-substrate data (human, phosphorylation only): 39,037 rows, giving 39,015 unique triplets. OmniPath combines PhosphoSitePlus, ProtMapper, MIMP, KEA, HPRD, phospho.ELM, SIGNOR, PhosphoNetworks, dbPTM, Reactome, NCI-PID, Li2012 and text-mined sources (REACH, Sparser, RLIMS-P, BEL).
2. SIGNOR direct download (human, protein-to-protein phosphorylation): 10,844 rows parsed, adding 1,140 new triplets. 4 more came from 3 rows with unusual residue formatting, recovered by hand.

Processing:
- Residues were converted to one-letter format (e.g. Thr307 -> T307).
- Entries were deduplicated by kinase|substrate|site, and all supporting databases were recorded for each.
- Heptameric peptides were taken as the central 7 residues of SIGNOR's 15-residue windows.

Limitations:
- Peptides are present for only 9,442 entries (about 24%). The PhosphoSitePlus download returned 0 entries, probably because it requires a login, so most entries lack a peptide.
- Some source credits are indirect. Derived tags such as HPRD_MIMP or SIGNOR_ProtMapper were credited to the first-named database (here HPRD and SIGNOR), which may overstate direct support from that database.
- 1,512 SIGNOR phosphorylation rows had no residue, so they could not form triplets and were excluded.
- Text-mined sources (REACH, Sparser, RLIMS-P, BEL) are included but are less reliable than curated records.
- Gene symbols were taken as given by each source and were not normalised, so the same triplet could appear twice under different symbols.
- No separate quality review was run.
